comment.description: What a file holds and how to read it, line by line.

specVersion.description: The version of the spec a file belongs to, as spec/spec.md states it: Semantic Versioning.

name.description: What an entry is about, unique in its file and its group.

wallClock.description: Where a file's wall clock starts, an RFC 3339 instant in UTC: both sides' test clocks start there.

advance.description: Milliseconds the given clock steps through, from due to due, its timers fired in their order.

wall.description: Milliseconds the wall clock moves alone, forward or back, as a clock set by hand moves.

timer.description: A timer armed on the side's given clock, due exactly these milliseconds from now.

duration.description: A duration a side is given, a bound or a timeout, in milliseconds as spec 1.4 holds one: 1 to 2^31 - 1.

clauses.description: The units of spec/spec.md an entry checks: a clause, 9.2; an item of its numbered list, 9.2.5; a row of its table, counted from 1, 15.6.8.

bytes.description: Bytes in hexadecimal, two capital digits each, spaces aside; a bar parts a header from what follows it.

u53.description: A 64-bit field, within the integers every language holds exactly: 0 to 2^53 - 1.

kind.description: REQUEST 16, RESULT 17, FAILURE 18, NOTIFICATION 19, CHUNK 20, CREDIT 21, CANCEL 22.

protocolCode.description: A code of the protocol, as spec/spec.md section 8 names them.

code.description: A failure's code, the protocol's or the procedure's own: never 0.

credential.description: A header's CREDENTIAL block, as spec 4.4 lays it out: its scheme, by name, or by its number for a scheme to come, and its credential. OPAQUE has its 16 bytes, never all zero; JWT, its token; NONE and ELSEWHERE, nothing; a scheme to come, its bytes, which may be none.

bytes.description: A session's token: 16 bytes in hexadecimal, two capital digits each, a space between, never all zero.

token.description: A token in JWS Compact Serialization, base64url and periods, a byte a character: 1 to 1,004 of them, the most a header leaves.

bytes.description: Its bytes in hexadecimal, two capital digits each, a space between: none to 1,004, the most a header leaves.
